claim: Supplying plausible cause hypotheses (one right, one wrong, with how-to-test steps) raised debugging success; the headline 'six-fold' is an odds ratio of 6.24 (p=0.03) from one lab study of 20 people, equal to about 80% vs 55% raw success. Gap check: 95% CI on the odds ratio is about 1.1 to 35 (my calculation), and Fisher exact on 16/20 vs 11/20 gives p about 0.18, so the effect is weak evidence at this N. Time to fix did not improve (p=0.61).
agent_test: Give the agent 0, 1 wrong, or 2 (1 right, 1 wrong) supplied hypotheses on seeded bugs at equal tokens; compare fix rate.

claim: Supplying fault locations (where, not why) did not improve hypothesis quality or fix rate in humans.
agent_test: Give the agent line-level locations only vs locations plus a cause; compare fix rate and wasted tokens.

claim: Unaided developers form few hypotheses (median about 1-2 per defect) and most are wrong at first: 11% correct at stage 1, 25% at stage 2, 39% at stage 3 at hypothesis level (not participant level).
agent_test: Log hypotheses at S3 before any test; score how many are correct and how many are generated; force a minimum of 3 distinct hypotheses and compare.

claim: Holding a correct hypothesis at stage 2 predicts fixing the defect (odds about 5x) but is not sufficient: 6 of 20 failures held it and could not implement a fix.
agent_test: Score the agent's diagnosis and repair separately; measure how often a correct diagnosis still gives a failed patch.

claim: Humans in naturalistic work rarely state formal testable hypotheses; they hold vague speculations and test by edit-and-run.
agent_test: Compare a forced hypothesis-prediction template with free-form reasoning at equal tokens.

claim: Debugging is dominated by a few long episodes; short episodes are edit-and-test and long ones use many activities.
agent_test: Check on agent traces whether a long tail of stuck episodes dominates token spend; test a trigger that changes strategy after N failed tests.

claim: A wrong or missing early hypothesis sends developers to wrong material and stalls them; novices are bound by early hypotheses (Vessey) while single-cause thinking caused misses on two-line fixes. LLM side: a wrong user-supplied cause cut SWE-bench Verified pass@1 by about 9 to 11% relative (XYEval), and small models shown their own failed code did worse than a fresh draw (Verma).
agent_test: On bugs needing two edits or having a decoy cause, test whether forcing a second hypothesis before the first test reduces fixation.

claim: Scientific-debugging loop for LLMs (hypothesis, prediction, experiment, observation, conclusion) matches plain prompting on repair counts while giving explanations: ARHE 187 vs 177 correct, Defects4J 1.2 76 vs 87, v2.0 113 vs 110, at about 5x the time.
agent_test: Run AutoSD-style loop vs plain resampling at equal token budget; the key question is whether it wins when tokens are equal.

claim: Real execution output must feed the hypothesis loop: with model-imagined debugger output, plausible-patch rate fell from 73% to 63% and the DONE signal reversed in meaning.
agent_test: Ablate real tool output vs model-simulated output in the same loop at equal tokens.

claim: Model self-diagnosis is the repair bottleneck: swapping GPT-4's own explanation for a human one lifted repair success from 33.3% to 52.6%, and GPT-4 gave obviously wrong feedback 32/80 times vs 7/80 for humans.
agent_test: Inject a gold diagnosis into the agent after S3 to measure the ceiling; then try to close it with sampling and selection.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without an external signal does not help and can hurt (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1); gains seen earlier used oracle labels.
agent_test: Compare revise-after-self-review with revise-after-real-test at equal tokens.

claim: Confirmation bias in hypothesis testing is common in LLMs; more negative (disconfirming) tests go with success, and prompt interventions raise rule discovery from 42% to 56%. Boundary: FalsifyBench restates that negative tests are required only when the hypothesis is narrower than the truth; transfer to code debugging is untested.
agent_test: In debugging, require one test that would refute the leading hypothesis before accepting it; compare to no such rule.

claim: Turning control to a debugger or execution traces helps strong models and can hurt weak ones; handing over the debugger after repeated failed rewrites beat both extremes (Claude 3.7 52.1% vs 48.4% vs 37.2%).
agent_test: Trigger instrumented testing only after k failed patches vs always vs never, at equal tokens.

claim: Iterative debugging effectiveness decays fast with attempts, and for small models (up to 3B) re-showing the failed attempt is worse than a fresh draw at equal budget (MBPP+, pass@1 .688 vs .749 at 1.5B; .709 vs .778 at 3B); by 7B the arms tie. Debugging Decay Index recovery by fresh start (72.56 to 82.82 for llama3.1:8b) points the same way. Frontier models untested.
agent_test: After 2-3 failed attempts, restart with a summary of rejected hypotheses only vs keep full history; compare.

claim: Locating the cause is harder than fixing it, and the failed runs of code agents often find the right file but fail at fine-grained reasoning.
agent_test: Split agent token spend between localise and fix; measure which stage fails.

claim: Interrogative debugging (why/why-not questions over a recorded execution) improved human debugging strongly in the authors' own studies (about 8x less time in Alice; 3x success and 2x speed in Java), but this is author-run and small.
agent_test: Give the agent a queryable execution trace with why-not queries vs breakpoints only.

claim: Automated suspiciousness lists do not help people much and were skipped non-linearly; seeing a faulty line did not mean recognising it as faulty.
agent_test: Give the agent a ranked suspect list with the true fault at rank 1 vs rank 7 vs rank 35; check whether performance changes.

claim: No study replays the supplied-hypothesis manipulation (correct vs wrong vs none, equal tokens) on an LLM. The nearest evidence is XYEval, which injects a wrong suggestion only: SWE-bench Verified pass@1 fell 77.2 to 68.8, 78.0 to 70.8, 79.8 to 71.4 (Gemini models). The correct-hint and no-hint arms at matched tokens are still missing.
agent_test: This is the test itself: supplied correct, wrong, none hypotheses on identical bugs.

claim: A wrong supplied cause lowers coding-agent success modestly on SWE-bench Verified (about 9 to 11% relative on three Gemini models) and much more on interactive or terminal tasks (up to 46.7%). Agents recovered part of it by running tests: even told to obey the wrong advice, they scored 50.2 to 60.6.
schema_part: G (anti-fixation) / O (check a supplied hypothesis by running it)
agent_test: Inject a wrong cause into SWE-bench-style tasks, with and without a rule to test the cause before editing; compare pass rate and tokens.

claim: A generic warning about misleading advice only partly offsets the harm on SWE-bench Verified (drop -10.9% to -11.1% for Gemini 3.1 Pro), while naming the exact wrong item removes it. A plain 'distrust the hint' prompt is therefore not a sufficient guardrail.
agent_test: Compare a distrust-the-hint prompt with a forced test-the-hint step on wrong-hint tasks.

claim: At equal output budget, a repair loop does not reliably beat plain resampling: self-repair was level or worse than i.i.d. sampling at small budgets (Olausson, older models), and blind resampling beat repair for 1.5B and 3B models (Verma). Feedback quality is the lever. No current-model SWE-bench test with equal tokens exists; SWE-Doctor and AutoSD cost 1.9x and about 5x their baselines.
agent_test: Run the agent's hypothesis loop against best-of-N at the same total tokens on the same SWE-bench subset.

claim: Diagnosis quality sets the repair ceiling: GPT-4 self-explanations were obviously wrong 32/80 times vs 7/80 for humans and never expressed doubt (0/80). Human feedback lifted repair 33.3 to 52.6. Whether generate-many-then-select closes this gap is untested.
agent_test: Ask for K hypotheses with confidences, pick by a cheap run, and compare with a single hypothesis at equal tokens.

claim: Hypothesis steps help localization in one agent system: removing hypothesis generation cut MAP from 0.407 to 0.379 (document) and 0.226 to 0.195 (method); removing investigation cut it more (0.360, 0.183). No study varies the number of hypotheses held, so the how-many question (gap 5) is open.
agent_test: Vary the number of live hypotheses (1, 2, 4) at equal tokens and log switch rate and wrong-fix rate.

claim: Negative (disconfirming) tests are only strictly required when the hypothesis is narrower than the true rule; when broader, positive tests can falsify. The Wason-style gain of disconfirming-test rules in LLMs has not been shown on code bugs.
agent_test: Label each hypothesis as too narrow or too broad and compare scope-matched test choice with always-disconfirm.
